prompt:
A clean, straight-on scan of a veterinary practice's printed discharge care sheet -- bright white paper, teal ink, heading left-aligned. Titled 'GOING HOME - CARE NOTES' with the small line 'Twelve numbered notes'. Print EXACTLY 12 numbered lines (1. to 12.), one care note per line, each at least NINE words long.

CRITICAL WRITING LAW: these fifteen words are BANNED and must not appear anywhere in the twelve notes: the, a, an, and, of, to, in, is, it, with, for, on, that, this, as. Every note must still read as an ordinary, natural, complete English sentence of at least NINE words -- a full instruction an owner could follow, not a clipped fragment and not a list of keywords. Compose the wording yourself so that not one of those fifteen words is needed.

Teal text on white paper, nothing else on the sheet.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a printed caption panel or bulletin with numbered lines of text. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the wording is correct, does the image DEPICT that -- a printed page carrying a numbered list of text lines? A photo, a scan or a clean page all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_evidence: This picture shows a printed page with hollow rectangles drawn on it, and a written list beside it. Is every hollow rectangle drawn around a numbered line of the page's own numbered list -- rather than around the heading, or sitting in blank paper with no text inside it? Answer yes or no only.

steps.read_crop: Copy out all the printed text on this page, exactly as it appears. Put each printed line on its own line of your answer, and keep that line's leading number (for example '3.') at the start of it. Copy every word letter for letter, even if a word looks misspelled, made-up or wrong -- do not correct it, complete it, translate it or improve it. Add nothing of your own and leave nothing out.

Transcribe this page word for word. Write one line of your answer for each line of printed text, beginning with that line's printed number. Spell every word exactly as it stands on the page, including any word that looks like nonsense or a mistake; never repair it. No commentary, no summary, no extra lines.

Read the printed page out line by line and copy each line exactly as printed. When a line starts with a number that is PRINTED on the page, keep that printed number at the front of it; when a line carries no printed number -- a heading, for instance -- copy it with no number in front. Never number the lines of your answer yourself and never add a number the page does not print. Spell every word exactly as printed. Print what is on the paper, not what you think it should say. Output nothing else.
